Hold the violin without tension so you can play for a long time without getting tired.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart · Rest the violin on your left collarbone and your jaw on the chin rest · Hold it for one minute without the left hand, only with the weight of your head · Relax your shoulders and neck and repeat three times
Hold the bow with a relaxed hand and rounded fingers.

Practise first with a pencil: bent thumb opposite the middle finger · Move to the bow: thumb between the frog and the stick, little finger curved on top of the stick · Hold the bow in the air for ten seconds without squeezing · Make small finger movements up and down
Make a clean sound with a straight bow, parallel to the bridge.

Set the metronome to 60 · Play each string (G, D, A, E) four beats down-bow and four beats up-bow · Keep the bow between the bridge and the fingerboard · Listen for a broken sound and adjust the weight of your arm
Tune the four strings on your own with the app tuner.
Start with A (440 Hz) · Use the fine tuners for small adjustments · Then tune D, G and E · Play two strings together to check the fifth
Place fingers 1, 2 and 3 with 2 and 3 together and in tune.
On the A string play A, B, C sharp and D · Check each note with the tuner · Repeat on the D string (D, E, F sharp, G) · Keep the fingers down as you go up
Play the one-octave D major scale in tune and in time.
Metronome at 60, one note per beat · Play the scale up and down three times · Move to two notes per beat when it sounds clean · Take care when crossing from the D string to the A string
Share out the bow so the sound stays even from start to end.
Metronome at 60 · Whole bow in four beats, then in two · Half bow (upper and lower half) in one beat · Listen that the sound does not fade at the end of the bow
Move between strings without noise, using the arm rather than the wrist.
Metronome at 72 · Alternate open A and E, two notes per beat · Bring the elbow to the level of the next string in advance · Repeat with D and A, then with G and D
Cover the violin from the G string to the E string with good intonation.
Metronome at 72, one note per beat · Play the scale up and down · Move to two and then four notes per beat · Note the pitches that drift and repeat them slowly
Control volume with bow weight, speed and contact point.
Play a long note piano near the fingerboard · Repeat forte moving towards the bridge · Make a crescendo and a diminuendo in a single bow · Practise on every string
Shift the hand to third position and back without losing intonation.

On the A string play D with the first finger in third position · Check with the tuner before going on · Practise the shift from first to third with the same finger, sliding gently · Play the D major scale starting in third position
Prepare the vibrato motion slowly and evenly.

Without the bow, rest the second finger on the A string · Move the hand towards the bridge and back, two motions per beat at 60 · Go up to three and four motions per beat · Add the bow only when the motion is smooth
